name: Tim Walz
role: Minnesota governor since 2019; US representative (2007–2019); 2024 Democratic vice-presidential nominee
summary: Walz is a progressive Democrat who combines public investment in schools, child poverty reduction and paid leave with support for unions, abortion and LGBT protections, gun restrictions and rapid clean-energy transition. He presents himself as pragmatic and bipartisan, funds police and rejects abolition and school vouchers.

universal-healthcare.rationale: In 2018 he called a MinnesotaCare buy-in a step toward single-payer and said it was irresponsible not to get everyone covered, and at the 2024 convention he named health care a human right; as governor he pursued a public option and defended the ACA rather than a fully state-guaranteed system.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: His 2018 campaign site called for a $15 minimum wage and he said he had backed $15 federally in Congress, though he called it an 'aspirational goal' at a press conference before reaffirming it.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: He says the wealthiest should pay their 'fair share', opposed tax cuts for the wealthiest and corporations, and in 2025 proposed closing loopholes the wealthy use; he does not call for a large across-the-board increase.

unions-good.rationale: He calls himself 'a union guy' in the debate and says in 2023 and 2024 that Minnesota is and will always be a labor state, tying public projects to union labor and expanding the right to organize.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He voted for the 2010 Wall Street reform law and at the 2024 convention attacked 'banks free to take advantage of customers' and 'corporations free to pollute'; in 2025 he said the federal government had switched sides to help corporations 'screw you over'.

cut-welfare.rationale: He defends Medicaid, free school meals and the child tax credit and says fraud should be answered by stopping criminals rather than cutting funding, though his 2025 budget slowed growth in human-services spending.

state-harmful.rationale: He says government should exist 'not to meddle in your life, but to make it easier' and defends an extensive state role in schools, health care and child support.

limit-guns.rationale: He backs universal background checks, a red flag law and bans on 'weapons of war', but says people 'can still keep your firearms' and that he is not infringing the Second Amendment.

empower-police-military.rationale: His 2023 budget proposed more than half a billion dollars in public safety funding so police and first responders have 'every resource they need', alongside gun restrictions.

rehabilitation.rationale: His cannabis policy expunges convictions and removes barriers to rejoining work and community life.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: As a congressman in 2012 he said he supports repealing DOMA and allowing same-sex couples to marry, and MPR reported in 2013 he had long supported same-sex marriage.

abortion-legal.rationale: In the debate he says abortion decisions are women's and their doctors' to make, that Roe should be restored, and that Minnesota 'restored Roe'; he signed the state's reproductive freedom law.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: He cites making Juneteenth a state holiday and 'facing up to our nation's entire history', and in 2019 said the state must tackle racial inequities.

free-trade.rationale: He voted against trade promotion authority in 2015, said in the debate that offshoring and right-to-work states hurt his communities while asking for 'fair trading partners', and CFR describes him as skeptical of some trade agreements; mixed with his efforts to expand trade with Canada and Europe.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: He opposed proposed Syria air strikes and sought to end support for Saudi Arabia’s Yemen war.

limit-growth.rationale: In the debate he said climate action and job creation are 'not a false choice' and he describes clean energy as an engine of jobs and growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He signed a law requiring 100 percent carbon-free electricity by 2040 and in the debate said reducing climate impact is 'absolutely critical' while backing large federal climate investment.

expand-nuclear.rationale: In 2009 as a congressman he joined Rep. Paulsen in calling to lift Minnesota's moratorium on new nuclear plants, saying a plant would raise output and cut emissions, but with concern about waste; no later position was found.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: In the debate he called Trump's trade war a loss and said tariffs would cost families $4,000, and in 2025 called the president's tariffs 'pointless' and a 'tariff tax', while still wanting manufacturing brought home through 'fair trading partners'.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He advocates state investment in green energy, innovation and the future AI economy.

democracy-best.rationale: In the debate he said 'democracy is bigger than winning an election', that you shake hands when you lose, and that settling differences at the ballot box matters even when the result is unwelcome.

political-violence-never.rationale: After the June 2025 assassination of Rep. Hortman he said 'we are not a country that settles our differences at gunpoint' and called on everyone to 'stand united against all forms of violence'.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: He celebrates returning the Upper Sioux Agency land to its Indigenous owners.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: He says Israel has 'the right to defend themselves', that the United States will stand by it, and calls for a sustainable two-state solution.

school-vouchers.rationale: He has repeatedly said private school vouchers and education savings accounts 'are not going to happen' and does not want public schools to lose funding.

national-self-determination.rationale: He says the Palestinian people have 'every right to life and liberty' and calls for moving toward a two-state solution.

night-watchman-state.rationale: He proposes state action in schools, child care, paid leave, health coverage and climate well beyond defence and justice.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He says 'nobody gets told they don't belong' and that freedom that is not for everybody 'is privilege'.

separated-powers.rationale: In 2025 he condemned a president who wants to be 'a king' and acting without due process, and in the debate he called Jan. 6 and refusal to accept an election a threat to the constitutional order.

priority-to-poor.rationale: He frames his child tax credit as focusing help 'on the families who need it most' and as cutting child poverty by a quarter to a third.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: He calls book bans censorship ('they're banning books') and contrasts them with Minnesota's approach; this concerns school book bans, which is nearby rather than identical.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: He said in 2024 'the Electoral College needs to go' and favoured a national popular vote, and as governor signed Minnesota into the National Popular Vote compact in 2023; his campaign said the remark was not its position.

corporate-influence.rationale: In the debate he said Trump took oil executives to Mar-a-Lago for campaign money in exchange for policy, and in 2025 said the federal government under Trump exists to help corporations at citizens' expense.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: He signed the 2023 trans refuge law protecting access to gender-affirming care, and in 2023 said 'that march stops at Minnesota's borders'; the protections he describes concern care and legal protection rather than legal recognition of gender.

social-market-economy.rationale: He pairs a 'pro-business' state with paid leave, child care and worker protections, arguing in the debate that Minnesota's paid leave helps employers retain workers.

racial-franchise.rationale: He rejects voting standards that deny rights based on race, colour or language.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: He voted yes on the 2010 Don't Ask, Don't Tell Repeal Act.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: He proposed record public safety funding for cities and counties and law enforcement resources, and calls for stopping criminals rather than cutting enforcement.

free-public-college.rationale: He cites free public tuition for low-income students (the North Star Promise) as an achievement, a means-tested rather than universal program.

collective-bargaining.rationale: In the debate he blamed right-to-work states and attacks on the 'right to collectively bargain' for weakening workers, and in 2024 he cited expanding the right to organize; he does not describe bargaining as the only way pay is set.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: He criticised right-to-work states as having made collective bargaining more difficult.

notes:
Independent second pass built from his five State of the State speeches (2019, 2022-2025), the Oct. 1, 2024 vice-presidential debate, his 2024 convention speech, House roll calls and reports of his own remarks. Searched for each theme; found nothing sourceable for markets, property, central planning, ownership and the many historical and ideological statements. Left null: the Minnesota governor's own site was blocked to automated fetching, so signing statements were not used; cannabis is not treated as an answer on drugs; the 'no guarantee of free speech' clip is disputed in context so hate speech is left null; death penalty, assisted dying, voter ID and student-loan cancellation rest only on secondary or compiled material. Several answers rest on laws a Democratic legislature passed and he signed, which are used only where he also spoke for them. His 2025 budget slowed human-services growth, so cut-welfare is -1 rather than -2.

Merged with an independent gpt-6.1-sol audit: 5 answers taken from it, 22 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

gpt-6.1-sol notes: All themes and remaining nulls reviewed against congressional history and 2025–2026 speeches. Most recent gun position supersedes earlier NRA support. Cannabis is the documented drug-policy exception, not support for every recreational drug. An AI advisory council does not establish a wish for algorithmic government; left null. Auditor identification: the runtime identifies this assistant as GPT-6/Codex but does not expose an exact version or variant; gpt-6 is the available identifier, not an asserted variant. Final wording review left nature-intrinsic-value, socialized-care unknown because the available record addresses a related, narrower or different proposition.
